The result is an RDKit Mol object, not SMILES. Need to convert to SMILES maybe using tool? Not provided. Could use map_reaction? Not. Maybe deprotect_molecule returns SMILES string? It returned Mol object; maybe we need to get its SMILES via RDKit but not available. Could use another tool? Not.

Maybe we can use detect_functional_groups on the deprotected mol? It expects SMILES string, not Mol. So need SMILES. Could use tool to convert Mol to SMILES? Not available.

Alternative: Use deprotect_molecule on second and third, but same issue.

Maybe deprotect_molecule returns a string representation? The result shows object, but maybe the tool returns SMILES string in result field? It shows object representation. Might need to convert using RDKit's MolToSmiles but not available.

We could instead use detect_protection_groups to see protecting groups and then manually remove? Could just infer that deprotected version removes the O[Si] group, giving O-H. So the deprotected SMILES would be same as precursor but with O instead of O[Si](...). So first precursor: O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C is a tert-butyldimethylsilyl (TBDMS). Removing gives OH. So deprotected SMILES: "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO". That matches second precursor (which already has O). Indeed second precursor is "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C". That's different location of silyl. Third has silyl on carboxylate.

Thus the core product likely is "C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO". That's the deprotected molecule (no silyl). Let's set target_smiles = that.

Now search template catalog with functional_groups_formed etc using this target.
